text:
Alice Nguyen: Quick sync — we need to lock the final set of runtime/infra metrics for the new ops console tiles. I'm proposing: latency_p50/p95, request_rate, token_throughput, cache_hit_rate, routing_fallbacks_count, and gpu_util. Thoughts?
Bob Patel: Add vendor_quantized_model_count and quantization_quality_regressions (for Optimize team alerts).
Caroline Mendez: +1 for cache_hit_rate. Also we should standardize exporter names to avoid collisions across services. Suggest: `redwood.runtime.<service>.<metric>` rather than mixing servicefirst and runtimefirst.
Ethan Ross: Agree on naming. Also, aggregation windows — we need 1m for alerting, 5m for dashboard smoothing, and 1h for long-term trends. Retention: raw 1m-series for 30d, 5m rollups 365d, 1h rollups forever (or N years).
Alice Nguyen: That matches my expectation. For rollout UX, product wants the per-route tile to show both p95 and fallback_rate with an inline note when a fallback happens in the last 10m. Can the telemetry team emit a `routing.fallback.last_event_ts`?
Caroline Mendez: We can emit a last_event_ts tag but avoid cardinality explosion. Better: incremental counter + last_event_bucket tag (0/1) per 1m series.
Bob Patel: For exporters — current runtime exporter is `runtime-exporter:1.3.0`. We need to coordinate a minor bump that adds quantized_model_count and cache_hit_rate. I can push a release on Wed if nobody objects. @SRE Oncall any deployment window constraints?
SRE Oncall: Wed midday looks fine, suggest toggling feature flag and reading metrics on staging for 24h before prod rollout.
DevBuildBot: CI pipeline triggered for branch feat/exporter-metrics. Build #482 queued.
Ethan Ross: On aggregation jobs: here's the pseudo-config I want for the hourly job — keeps it idempotent and safe for backfills:
```
job: rollup_hourly
inputs: ["redwood.runtime.*.1m"]
aggregate: {method: avg, window: "1h"}
output: "redwood.rollup.1h.%{service}.%{metric}"
retention_days: 3650
backfill_safe: true
concurrency: 8
```
Caroline Mendez: Looks good. For backfill plan: do we want to backfill the last 90 days of 1m -> 5m and 1h rollups? Backfill cost estimate: ~1200 GPU-minutes if we run at concurrency 8 across shard cluster.
Bob Patel: Can we limit backfill to customer-priority services first? We have cost constraints. Suggest tiered backfill: prod-critical (last 90d), core infra (30d), others no backfill.
Alice Nguyen: OK. Product agrees on tiered backfill. We need a list of prod-critical services by EOD Friday. @Caroline can you draft a short policy and endpoint tag to mark services?
Caroline Mendez: Yup. Drafting `telemetry.backfill_tier` tag with values `critical|core|none`. Will push spec to the docspace later today.
Ethan Ross: One more thing — quotas. Aggregation job should respect per-tenant throughput limits so we don't blow customer quotas during backfill. Add per-tenant rate limiter in the job.
SRE Oncall: Also add circuit breaker: if ingest error rate > 2% across exporters, pause backfill and notify #incidents.
Bob Patel: Implementation plan: 1) exporter PR adds metrics + backfill_tier tag 2) rollup job PR adds rate-limiter + backfill safe flag 3) run staging for 24h 4) schedule backfill for critical services in weekend window 5) monitor cost/alerts, expand slowly.
Alice Nguyen: Timeline: exporter PR by Wed, rollup job PR by Thu, staging test Fri, backfill Sat-Sun for critical. Can everyone confirm?
Bob Patel: Confirmed.
Caroline Mendez: Confirmed. Draft will include sample tags and example prometheus config snippet.
Ethan Ross: Confirmed but will need a short runbook for pausing backfill mid-flight. I'll write that.
SRE Oncall: I'll create an alerting dashboard panel to watch ingest error rate + backfill throughput.
Alice Nguyen: Awesome. Action items: Bob — exporter PR; Caroline — tag spec + doc; Ethan — backfill runbook; SRE Oncall — alert dashboard + deployment window. I'll file a follow-up in the tracker's epic and ping infra to reserve the weekend slot. Thanks all :thumbsup:
